title: Sidecar control protocol sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory sketch for a small, dependable control API used by app processes to manage a local/private inference sidecar. Goal: minimal surface area, easy to embed into existing apps, works over unix domain socket and loopback. This is a working scratchpad — lots of open questions below.

High level goals / constraints:
- Single-process app should be able to start/stop and query a sidecar with a tiny HTTP-ish JSON protocol.
- Support both local unix socket (recommended) and 127.0.0.1:port for environments that need it.
- Authentication should be pluggable but default to no-auth in dev; provide optional token or TLS+mTLS for private deployments.
- Keep control plane separate from data-plane (prediction) so health/control calls never block model inference.
- Small binary-compatible semantics so teams can implement phony sidecar (mock) for tests.

API surface (v0 sketch):
Base: unix:///var/run/redwood-sidecar.sock or http://127.0.0.1:2368
All endpoints accept/return JSON; Content-Type: application/json.  Responses: {"ok": true, "code": 200, "body": ...} envelope for forward compatibility.

1) GET /v0/info
- Purpose: discover sidecar capabilities and config
- Response.body: {"version": "0.1.0", "models": [{"id":"redwood-1.0-q4_0","max_tokens":2048, "quantized":true}], "modes": ["predict","stream","embed"], "uptime_s": 234} 
- Notes: include optional runtime hints (gpu_count, fp16_supported) later.

2) POST /v0/control/start
- Purpose: request sidecar to load model / initialize context
- Request.body: {"model_id":"redwood-1.0-q4_0", "load_options": {"max_context":4096, "quant_profile":"8bit"}, "ticket":"optional-op-id"}
- Response.body: {"load_id":"uuid-xxx", "status":"loading"}
- Idempotency: POST with same ticket should return same load_id/status.

3) POST /v0/control/stop
- Request.body: {"load_id":"uuid-xxx", "graceful": true}
- Response.body: {"status":"stopped"}

4) GET /v0/control/status?load_id=uuid-xxx
- Response.body: {"status":"loaded|loading|failed|stopped", "metrics": {"mem_mb": 4500, "active_sessions": 2}}

5) POST /v0/predict (data-plane doorway to inference)
- Purpose: single-shot call for non-streaming predictions (apps will prefer streaming where supported)
- Request.body: {"load_id":"uuid-xxx", "input": {"prompt":"Translate to fr: Hello world", "max_tokens":128, "temperature":0.0}, "metadata": {"request_id":"req-123"}}
- Response.body: {"output": "Bonjour le monde", "tokens": 3, "latency_ms": 140}

6) POST /v0/stream (websocket or chunked HTTP)
- For streaming tokens, negotiate via /v0/info which modes are supported.

Control vs Data separation notes:
- /v0/control/* endpoints MUST be handled by a lightweight thread/loop that cannot be starved by long-running inference ops. Implementation note: accept control requests on a distinct listener (same socket OK) but dispatch to control worker.
- For unix sockets, prefer file mode 0660 with group=redwood to restrict local access.

Socket binding strategy (dev vs prod):
- Dev: create ephemeral dir in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or /tmp/redwood-sidecar-$UID, socket name 'sidecar.sock', no systemd integration.
- Prod-private: accept configured path (e.g., /var/run/redwood/$APP/sidecar.sock) with systemd unit that owns the dir.
- When using TCP, listen only on localhost. Consider using a generated bearer token for additional local auth.

Example interaction (ASCII):
[app process] <--> unix socket (/var/run/sidecar.sock) <--> [sidecar daemon] <-> (inproc/IPC) <-> [inference worker(s)/GPU]

Sketch of minimal JSON schema for predict call (proto-like):
- predict_request := {"load_id": string, "input": {"type":"text","text": string}, "options": {"max_tokens": int, "stop": [string], "temperature": float}, "metadata": { ... }}
- predict_response := {"ok": bool, "code": int, "body": {"output": string, "usage": {"tokens": int}, "meta": {"model": string, "latency_ms": int}}}

Edge cases and open questions (TODO):
- Multi-tenancy: if a sidecar hosts multiple app processes (shared socket), how to enforce per-app quotas? scope by token? by uid? Need policy.
- Hot reloads: what happens to in-flight streaming requests during model reload? Provide a graceful fallback header? suggestion: return 409+retry-after for new streams while draining existing ones.
- Backpressure: if app floods predict, sidecar should either queue up to N requests or return 429. Need default N (maybe 64) and a tunable queue policy.
- Heap vs GPU memory accounting: expose a best-effort memory footprint for loaded model, must warn if host underprovisioned.
- Security model: default dev no-auth is convenient but dangerous in corporate envs. Provide simple token file (/run/sidecar-token) readable by app or use mTLS. Document recommended patterns for private deployments.

Implementation notes for prototype:
- Build HTTP layer using small embedded server (rust: hyper or axum; go: fasthttp/net/http) with unix socket support.
- Control thread should be <128KB stack and only touch in-memory structures; inference tasks posted to worker pool.
- Provide small shim in SDKs (python/go/node) that auto-discovers socket and retries for startup race. SDK should implement helper: ensure_loaded(model_id) that calls start + polls status.

Testing checklist (prototype):
- [ ] unit tests for idempotent start semantics (ticket-based)
- [ ] integration test: app <-> sidecar over unix socket, simulate model load and predict
- [ ] fuzz test: send random JSON to control endpoints and ensure sidecar stays up
- [ ] stress test: N=200 concurrent predict calls, measure 95th p99 latencies and correct 429 behavior

Notes / references:
- Related tickets: JIRA-PLATFORM-3421 (sidecar auth model), JIRA-OPS-4110 (systemd deployment pattern)
- proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar-proto/pull/78 (initial api shape, WIP)
- Slack thread: #sidecar-proto (design conv on 2025-10-28)

Open decisions for next pass:
1) Should control endpoints use the same socket as data-plane? pros: single path, cons: potential interference and permission mixing. Recommendation: same socket but separate request queue + prioritization.
2) Idempotency token semantics for start: use 'ticket' from client or generate server-side? Prefer client-provided ticket for test determinism.
3) Default behavior for model eviction under memory pressure: LRU across load_id or explicit operator action? Lean to explicit eviction with operator signals.

Immediate next steps (personal TODOs):
- turn predict/poll schemas into JSON Schema file and push to repo (next week)
- spike: implement a tiny rust prototype listening on unix socket that responds to /v0/info and /v0/predict with canned outputs (2d day effort)
- sync with Priya and Liam next Tuesday to align on auth model and plugin surface

Random brain-dump thoughts:
- Could expose small CLI wrapper 'sidecarctl' for ops to inspect socket easily (sidecarctl status --socket /path)
- Consider an env-based discovery for SDKs: REDWOOD_SIDECAR_SOCKET=/path or REDWOOD_SIDECAR_TCP=127.0.0.1:2368
- Backwards compatibility: reserve /v0 prefix; allow a /v0/meta endpoint for debug dumps (stack traces, loaded libs) gated to local root or token.

If nothing else, this doc should serve as the canonical dev scratchpad for the week while I prototype. Will iterate after prototyping and actual API feedback.
